supports.excerpt:
Learning from human feedback is crucial in aligning large language models (LLMs) with human
                                        values and intentions [51], ensuring they are helpful, honest, and harmless [5]. Reinforcement learning
                                        from human feedback (RLHF) [18, 62, 73] is a popular method for fine-tuning language models
                                        to achieve effective alignment. While the classical RLHF approach [62, 70] has shown impressive
                                        results, it presents optimization challenges due to its multi-stage procedure, which involves training a
                                        reward model and then optimizing a policy model to maximize that reward [13].
                                        Recently, researchers have been exploring simpler offline algorithms. Direct Preference Optimization
                                        (DPO) [66] is one such approach. DPO reparameterizes the reward function in RLHF to directly
                                        learn a policy model from preference data, eliminating the need for an explicit reward model. It has
                                        gained widespread practical adoption due to its simplicity and stability. In DPO, the implicit reward
                                        is formulated using the log ratio of the likelihood of a response between the current policy model and
                                        the supervised fine-tuned (SFT) model. However, this reward formulation is not directly aligned with

                                                Code and models can be found at https://github.com/princeton-nlp/SimPO.

Figure 1: SimPO and DPO mainly differ in their reward formulation, as indicated in the shaded box.
SimPO outperforms DPO significantly across a range of settings on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard.

skill_drafts.name: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) Policy Learning
skill_drafts.description: A simplified offline algorithm for fine-tuning language models directly from preference data without requiring an explicit reward model. Uses log-ratio of policy and reference model likelihoods to formulate implicit rewards.
skill_drafts.objective: Align language models with human preferences through direct policy optimization
applicable_signals: Preference pairs available from human feedback or comparative evaluations
Need to fine-tune LLM without training a separate reward model
Seeking simpler, more stable alternative to multi-stage RLHF
Offline learning scenario with fixed preference dataset
contraindications: Do not use if explicit reward model is already trained and validated
Do not use if online RL feedback collection is feasible and preferred
Do not use if reward function must be independently interpretable for compliance or auditing
Do not use if preference data is sparse or unreliable
intervention_moves: Prepare preference dataset with chosen and rejected response pairs
Initialize policy model from supervised fine-tuned (SFT) baseline
Compute log-ratio of policy and reference model likelihoods for each pair
Formulate implicit reward using the log-ratio parameterization
Optimize policy to maximize preference-aligned implicit reward
Evaluate on held-out preference test set
triggers: Need to fine-tune LLM from preference pairs without training separate reward model; seeking simpler alternative to multi-stage RLHF
constraints: Requires a reference SFT model as baseline for likelihood computation
Requires preference pairs (chosen vs. rejected responses) as training data
Implicit reward formulation is tied to log-ratio; cannot be extracted or inspected independently
Offline setting: no online interaction or iterative feedback collection
cautions: Implicit reward may not align with explicit human values if preference data is biased
Log-ratio formulation assumes reference model is a reasonable baseline; poor SFT initialization may degrade results
Preference pairs must be comparable (same prompt, different responses) for meaningful optimization
output_contract: Fine-tuned policy model that ranks preferred responses higher than dispreferred ones on held-out preference test set. Model should demonstrate improved alignment with human preferences compared to the SFT baseline.

metadata.prompt: Apply DPO to fine-tune a policy model from preference pairs. Reparameterize the reward function using the log ratio of likelihood between the current policy model and a supervised fine-tuned (SFT) reference model. Train the policy to maximize the implicit reward derived from this formulation, eliminating the need for a separate reward model training stage.

skill_drafts.name: Reward Formulation via Policy-Reference Log Ratio
skill_drafts.description: Compute implicit reward signals using the log ratio of likelihood between a current policy model and a supervised fine-tuned reference model. This micro-skill eliminates the need for an explicit reward model in preference-based learning by directly scoring response pairs.
skill_drafts.objective: Compute implicit reward signal from model likelihood ratios without explicit reward model
applicable_signals: Supervised fine-tuned reference model likelihood estimates
contraindications: Reward function must be human-interpretable or auditable
Explicit reward model already available and preferred for other pipeline stages
Likelihood estimates are unreliable or model outputs are unstable
workflow_steps: Obtain likelihood of response under current policy model
Obtain likelihood of same response under supervised fine-tuned reference model
Return scalar reward score for preference pair
triggers: Implementing Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) or similar offline preference learning
Need to score response pairs without training a separate reward model
Preference data available but explicit reward model not required
constraints: Both policy and reference model must be available and comparable
Likelihood estimates must be computed on the same response samples
Log ratio computation requires valid probability values from both models
cautions: Implicit reward formulation may not align directly with human preference intent in all domains
Numerical stability of log ratios depends on model calibration
output_contract: Scalar reward score per response pair that correlates with human preference labels; suitable for downstream preference optimization steps

metadata.prompt: Calculate the implicit reward for a response pair by taking the log ratio of the likelihood under the current policy model to the likelihood under the supervised fine-tuned reference model. Use this scalar reward to score preference comparisons without training a separate reward model.
